Quota, usage and cost in OpenCode TUI and Desktop.

--- ## Install ```bash opencode plugin add @slkiser/opencode-quota ``` Restart OpenCode and type `/quota`. A window opens with your limits. Click a tab (Usage, Limits, Plugin, or a Settings tab) or press `tab` to move between them; click or press `esc` to close it. > [!IMPORTANT] > You need OpenCode `2.0.26+`; the terminal commands also need Node.js `22.13+` or `23.4+`. > [!NOTE] > Still on OpenCode 1? Run `npx @slkiser/opencode-quota@4 init` instead, and see the [OpenCode 1 README](https://github.com/slkiser/opencode-quota/blob/release/4.x/README.md).
Edit opencode.json yourself Add the plugin to `opencode.jsonc` or `opencode.json`, and keep your other plugins. In `~/.config/opencode` it works in every project; in a project's folder, only there. This one entry loads both the server and the TUI: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["@slkiser/opencode-quota"], } ```
## What you get - **TUI:** a `/quota` window, a sidebar panel, a status line and toasts. - **Desktop (experimental, OpenCode `2.2.0+`):** a side tab, pills, a bottom strip, toasts, a usage window (**Quota** command) and a settings page. Turn it off in **Settings → Extensions → Plugins**.
Where each setting shows in the TUI and in Desktop
Setting groupTUIDesktop
sidebarQuota panel in the sidebarQuota side tab
collapsedSidebar panel folded to one line per providerTitlebar pill, and the Quota side tab when folded
statusLineLine under the message boxStrip at the bottom of the window, and the pill above the message box
toastToasts with barsToasts with the Quota side tab's rows and bars; a reset notice is a sentence

Note: in the TUI the status line hides while the sidebar shows quota, unless Next to the sidebar (statusLine.withSidebar) is on. In Desktop the strip also shows next to the Quota side tab by default; Next to the side panel (statusLine.withSidePanel) turns that off. statusLine.composerPill: false (Pill above the message box) hides only the pill in Desktop.

- **Web:** `/quota`, `/quota_usage` and `/quota_status` post a report in the chat. The AI never sees it. - **Terminal:** `npx @slkiser/opencode-quota@latest show`, even with OpenCode closed. - **Scripts and status bars:** JSON, an export file and metrics ([how](docs/readme/external-integration.md)). - **Live settings** in every open OpenCode. ## Commands | Command | What it shows | | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/quota` | Limits. Web and Desktop: limits next to the last 7 days of usage | | `/quota_usage [range]` | Tokens and API cost: `today` (default), `24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `90d`, `all`, `session` (with its subagents), `between` two dates | | `/quota_status` | Setup check: logins, providers, pricing, and notices | | `/quota_settings` | Settings tabs (TUI only) | For example `/quota_usage 30d` or `/quota_usage between 2026-09-01 2026-09-25`. In a terminal, with OpenCode open or closed, `npx @slkiser/opencode-quota@latest show` shows your quota and `npx @slkiser/opencode-quota@latest status` checks your setup ([how they differ](docs/readme/troubleshooting.md#terminal-commands)). Add `--help` to see all options. ## Settings - Change settings in `/quota_settings` (TUI) or the Quota page in Desktop's settings. Both save to `opencode-quota/settings.jsonc` in OpenCode's config folder and keep your comments. - Custom providers, the Claude CLI path and the export path are set only in the file. - The `┃` in a bar marks even use until the reset. **Even-use mark** (`layout.evenUse`) turns it off. - [Settings and defaults](docs/readme/configuration.md) ## Providers Log in with `/connect` and the provider shows up. Switch providers on or off in `/quota_settings` → **Providers**.

# Provider template

Copy this folder when adding a provider that should use the README wording:

```text
Existing OpenCode auth, global config, or env
```

This template is outside `src/` and is not published to npm. `package.json` only publishes `dist`, `README.md`, and `LICENSE`.

## Who this is for

Use this template for API-key/token providers that support all three trusted sources:

1. existing OpenCode API-key/token login, read through the plugin API
2. trusted user/global OpenCode config
3. environment variables

Do not use it for OAuth-only providers such as OpenAI.

Auth is part of the provider's entry in `src/lib/provider-registration.ts`, not a new file: its `apiKey` lists the env var names and OpenCode provider ids. The shared resolver reads env, then trusted global config, then OpenCode logins for those ids, and `tests/lib.api-key-resolver.test.ts` covers that order; add a row to its vendor table.

## Copy targets

| Template file      | Copy to                              | Purpose                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider.ts`      | `src/providers/<provider>.ts`        | Ask the API, turn its reply into rows, say when it is available. |
| `provider.test.ts` | `tests/providers.<provider>.test.ts` | Prove the rows, the error and availability through fake HTTP.    |

Also update:

- `src/lib/provider-registration.ts`: one entry, in display order, with the provider's label, OpenCode ids, row keys (`rowKeys`) and key (`apiKey`)
- `src/providers/registry.ts`: bind the provider to its id (the compiler checks every id has one)
- `src/lib/quota-status.ts`: its `DEBUG_DETAILS` entry, `{}` when no debug detail needs redacting (the compiler checks this too)
- `tests/lib.api-key-resolver.test.ts`: a row in its vendor table
- `README.md`

## Replacement checklist

Before coding, replace these placeholders everywhere:

- `example-provider`
- `Example Provider`
- `EXAMPLE_PROVIDER_API_KEY`
- `exampleProvider`
- `exampleProviderProvider`
- `queryExampleRows`
- `https://api.example.com/v1/usage`

## README wording rule

Use `Existing OpenCode auth, global config, or env` only after tests prove all three paths work. Do not leave copied template tests skipped, todo-only, or unresolved. If one path is missing, use provider-specific wording instead.

In provider ledgers, use `Data from` rather than `Source`. These are friendly labels, not exact internal result types: use `Quota` as the umbrella for quota and rate-limit windows, join other multiple results with `and`, and use `Quota and usage` in that order. Keep exact internal `type` values in code and JSON/export documentation.

## Row rule

A provider returns the row contract in `src/providers/contract.ts`: per account, its rows and its errors, plus debug details for `/quota_status`. The copied `provider.ts` shows one remote quota row with the percent left (`quotaRow`). Keep that shape when the provider only reports a percentage.

Each row's `key` becomes its id (`example-provider.monthly`), which users' hide, rename and order settings use, so a key never changes once released. List every key in the provider's `rowKeys`; `fetchRows` in the provider tests fails on a key that is not listed.

If the provider reports more than a percentage, follow `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`: amounts as typed `used`, `limit`, `remaining` or `amount` values, yes/no as `flag`, never pre-formatted money strings.

# Upstream Plugin References

This directory stores committed local copies of the published npm packages tracked by the upstream plugin maintenance workflow.

Tracked packages:

- `cursor-opencode-provider` (npm `latest`)
- `opencode-gemini-auth` (npm `latest`, the OpenCode 2 line since 2.x)
- `@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth` (npm `alpha`, the OpenCode 2 build; tracked internally under `.github/scripts/upstream-plugins/opencode-agy-auth/`)

Each package follows the npm dist-tag set in `.github/scripts/lib/upstream-plugin-specs.mjs`.

Companion identities are verified against npm package metadata and their canonical GitHub repositories.

Refresh everything with:

```sh
pnpm run upstream:sync
```

Prepare a full review handoff with:

```sh
pnpm run upstream:prepare-review
```

Check whether GitHub should open or close `[check] <plugin> had update` issues with:

```sh
pnpm run upstream:check
```

The published package contents under each plugin directory are regenerated by the sync script. Edit the scripts, not the copied package files.

Known embedded credentials from upstream packages are deterministically redacted during sync before the snapshots are committed. Update checks still come from `.github/scripts/upstream-plugins/lock.json` version comparisons, not from sanitized file contents.

The GitHub issue stays open until the maintainer closes it manually after review/fix/release work.

# cursor-opencode-provider

Use [Cursor](https://cursor.com) subscription models from [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and compatible coding agents by speaking Cursor's Connect-RPC agent protocol.

This project is a custom **AI SDK provider** (`LanguageModelV3`) plus an **OpenCode plugin** that handles authentication and model discovery. Instead of calling a generic chat-completions API, it encodes and decodes Cursor's protobuf agent protocol over HTTP/2 to Cursor's agent backend.

> **Runs unchanged across OpenCode, OpenCode 2.x, and five additional coding agents.** OpenCode loads this plugin natively, including through the dedicated OpenCode 2.x entrypoint. [OCP — OpenCode Plugin Compatibility](https://github.com/oakimov/opencode-plugin-compat) runs the same published plugin, without a provider fork, in **Kilo Code, MiMo Code, pi, oh-my-pi, and DeepSeek Harness**. See [Coding-agent compatibility](#coding-agent-compatibility).
>
> **Status:** Usable end-to-end for authentication, model discovery, streaming, and tools. See [Known limitations](#known-limitations).

## Features

- **Multi-host compatibility** — the same plugin package runs natively in OpenCode and OpenCode 2.x, and unchanged through OCP in Kilo Code, MiMo Code, pi, oh-my-pi, and DeepSeek Harness; new host support belongs in the compatibility layer rather than a provider fork
- **OpenCode integration** — registers a `cursor` provider with auth hooks and cached model list
- **Authentication** — browser OAuth (PKCE), or API key from [cursor.com/settings](https://cursor.com/settings)
- **Model discovery** — fetches available models from Cursor's API and caches them locally
- **Image input** — advertises vision only for supported models and forwards OpenCode image attachments to Cursor
- **Streaming** — bidirectional Connect-RPC Runs with stale-session rotation, health checks, semantic/read-idle deadlines, bounded replay-safe recovery, and activity-aware held tool continuations
- **Tool calls** — maps Cursor exec-server messages to AI SDK / OpenCode tool-call parts using only the advertised canonical catalog. Exact advertised subagent names win; standard Cursor roles select compatible OpenCode agents, and native Task maps to OpenCode 1.x `task` or OpenCode 2.x `subagent`. OCP translates any alternate host vocabulary before it reaches this package. The bridge also covers Cursor's typed read/bash/edit/write/grep/find/ls request/result range, mirrors finalized display-only todo/plan state, and strips OpenCode 1.x and OpenCode 2.x read envelopes before returning content to Cursor.
- **Thinking / reasoning** — surfaces extended-thinking deltas where the model supports it

OpenCode 2.1.4 waits for cold-cache model discovery and publication during plugin
activation, with a 10-second readiness budget. Warm-cache startup uses the saved
inventory. Discovery failures leave authentication and later retries available;
see [model startup and diagnostics](docs/opencode-2.md#how-models-register-current).

## OpenCode setup

Host config, auth commands, and local-clone wiring differ by major version — follow [OpenCode 1.x](docs/opencode-1.md) or [OpenCode 2.x](docs/opencode-2.md).

### Authenticate

| Host | How |
|------|-----|
| **OpenCode 1.x** | `opencode auth login` → **cursor** ([details](docs/opencode-1.md#authenticate)) |
| **OpenCode 2.x** | `/connect` → **Cursor** ([details](docs/opencode-2.md#authenticate)). `CURSOR_API_KEY` is also picked up automatically. |

Then choose a method:

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Cursor account (browser login)** | PKCE OAuth — opens cursor.com to sign in |
| **API key** | Paste a key from [cursor.com/settings](https://cursor.com/settings) (`crsr_...`) |

After login, the plugin fetches your available models and writes them to `<host-cache>/cursor-models.json`. On later startups, a missing, empty, expired, or old-schema cache is refreshed during config load when Cursor auth is available; an existing stale cache remains usable if refresh fails. Completed conversation state is stored separately under `<host-cache>/cursor-conversations/`, with one independently replaced gzip-compressed protobuf snapshot per stable host session. Snapshots are refreshed at each successful Cursor `TurnEnded`, while a turn waits on a host tool, and when OpenCode 2.x stops a turn or shuts down, and restored on demand after provider restarts. A session loads only its own snapshot; it never waits for a directory-wide cleanup. Records not updated for more than 24 hours are rejected on load and collected independently using bounded reads of their persisted metadata, without relying on filesystem modification times; the same age rule collects temp files left by an interrupted save. Full payload and gzip integrity checks run when a snapshot is restored. Cursor's checkpoint is an index of content-addressed KV blobs rather than a self-contained transcript, so the snapshot retains the blobs reachable from the latest checkpoint and discards superseded blobs. This private Cursor state is not a copy of the host's session database.

### Paths (host cache)

Model/version caches and Cursor project metadata live under a **host cache root**, resolved in this order:

1. Explicit `createCursor({ cacheDir })` / host API cache override
2. A structural host path bridge installed before the provider loads
3. Native OpenCode: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/opencode`, otherwise `~/.cache/opencode`

The provider never detects or names fork hosts. Compatibility layers own host identity and may inject cache, data, and config roots through the structural bridge; without one, standalone OpenCode behavior is unchanged.

| Kind | Default (OpenCode) | Notes |
|------|--------------------|-------|
| Model, version, and 24-hour conversation **cache** | `~/.cache/opencode/` | A host bridge may replace the root |
| Cursor **project metadata** (`agent-tools`, terminals, …) | `~/.cache/opencode/projects/<slug>/` | under `<host-cache>/projects/` |
| OpenCode **auth** (`auth.json`) | `~/.local/share/opencode/` | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/` when set |
| OpenCode **config** (AGENTS, skills, …) | `~/.config/opencode/` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/` when set, as OpenCode resolves it |

### Select a model

Pick a model from the cached list (for example `composer-2.5`, `default`, or a Claude/GPT model exposed by your subscription):

```bash
opencode run --model cursor/composer-2.5 "Hello from Cursor via OpenCode"
```

#### Variants

Cursor models often expose parameterized variants (effort, thinking, fast, context tier, …). The plugin materializes those as OpenCode **model variants**. In the TUI, pick one from the variant dialog or cycle with OpenCode’s `variant_cycle` keybind (default `ctrl+t`).

The selected variant’s Cursor parameter map is forwarded on the Run as `requested_model.parameters` (isolated under `providerOptions.cursor.cursorVariantParameters` so unrelated OpenCode options are not leaked onto the wire). The provider validates that explicit selection against the current cached tuple; malformed, duplicate-id, or stale selections fail clearly instead of silently falling back to another variant. Parameter order does not matter.

Without an explicit selection, an effort hint stays within the requested base or max tier and changes only the effort of that tier's default variant (thinking and other parameters keep the default's values). The provider prefers non-Fast variants within that tier and keeps Cursor's declared default effort when the default is Fast. An unavailable effort falls back to an advertised default tuple rather than inventing parameter values.

#### 1M / long context

OpenCode’s context limit is static per model entry, while Cursor’s long-context tier is a variant parameter (`context=1m`). When a model has both a base tier and a `1m` tier, the plugin emits a separate OpenCode entry `<model-id>-1m` (for example `claude-opus-4-8-1m`) with:

- `limit.context` set to the 1M window (so overflow checks and compaction match the tier)
- `limit.output` set to `128000` (max generation tokens — not the context window; base entries use `32000`)
- only the long-context variants in its picker
- the real Cursor model id carried in `options.cursorModelId` (not `config.id`, which would make OpenCode merge base variants into the 1M entry)

The Run still uses Cursor’s original model id; OpenCode’s synthetic `-1m` id is only for picking and limits.

Other advertised max-context tiers also get separate entries. For example,
Grok 4.7's marked 500k variants appear under `grok-4.7-500k`, with a 500,000-token
context limit; `grok-4.7-500k-fast` carries the Fast variants and pricing.
Each dedicated context entry keeps only its tier's variants and retains the declared default
effort, including when the default's non-Fast twin is needed. Non-1M entries
retain the base output limit of 32,000 tokens.

Existing non-1M variant names also remain on the original base/Fast entries so
saved selections such as `grok-4.7#Grok 4.7 High 500k` keep working after an
upgrade. These legacy selections send the selected 500k parameters and max-mode
flag, but keep the original entry's conservative static context budget. Select
`grok-4.7-500k` or `grok-4.7-500k-fast` to give OpenCode the full 500k budget.

#### Fast variants with distinct prices

When Cursor publishes a different Fast rate for a model (currently Composer and Grok), the plugin emits a separate OpenCode entry `<model-id>-fast` (for example `composer-2.5-fast`) using the same pattern as `-1m`:

- only the Fast variants in its picker, with `" Fast"` in the catalog name
- the real Cursor model id in `options.cursorModelId`, plus default Fast variant parameters
- its own `cost` row (`composer-2.5-fast` is not nested under `composer-2.5`)

Claude Fast variants stay on the base entry: Cursor does not publish a separate Fast price for them, so they remain picker variants instead of a second catalog id. Combinations with long context use `<id>-1m-fast`.

#### Context limit sources

The provider resolves each catalog context limit in this order:

1. Live `AvailableModels` metadata (variant `context` parameters first, then context-limit fields)
2. Cursor’s published model table, generated from [`docs.md`](https://cursor.com/docs.md) alongside pricing data
3. A conservative `200000` fallback when neither source publishes a limit

The docs fallback only fills static catalog metadata. It does not invent Cursor variants or enable a long-context tier that `AvailableModels` did not advertise.

OpenCode 2.x can summarize with another provider's model. A committed summary
rebases the next Cursor turn onto compacted host history; failed or unused
background summaries keep the warm conversation. The requirement survives
restart. See [foreign compaction](docs/opencode-2.md#compaction-with-another-provider).

#### Model families

Catalog entries derive a models.dev-style `family` from the Cursor model id (`claude-haiku-4-5` → `claude-haiku`, `gpt-5.6-luna` → `gpt-luna`). Version segments and trailing `-1m` / `-fast` suffixes do not split families; Kimi keeps its major generation (`kimi-k2.7-code` → `kimi-k2`). Auto (`default`) has no derived family. A non-empty family supplied in cached model metadata takes precedence; the live `AvailableModels` schema has no family field.

OpenCode uses family metadata to select a small model for session titles (2.x: `gpt-luna`, `gemini-flash-lite`, `gemini-flash`, `claude-haiku`; 1.x: `gemini-flash`, `gpt-nano`, `claude-haiku`). If no eligible family is available, titles fall back to the session model. To override this selection, set the `title` agent's `model` on either major, or `small_model` on 1.x. Compaction summaries use the host's compaction model selection; this metadata does not move them to the small model. OpenCode 2.x's model-listing tool shows one entry per family unless asked for all.

- **Oversized / incomplete checkpoint graphs warn but do not remint** — before reusing a checkpoint, the provider measures its reachable KV graph. State above 100 MiB (Cursor CLI export/transfer budget) or an incomplete graph is logged (`action=warm-reuse`) and the sticky conversation is kept, matching CLI soft-reuse. KV, request-context, MCP-state, interaction, and heartbeat writes are ordered per Run and await HTTP/2 drain, so a large blob reply cannot create an unbounded queue later misreported as heartbeat backpressure. Uploads have no fixed drain deadline; stream termination and the read-idle watchdog bound failed connections. Stopping a turn cancels its initial, tool-result, or replacement upload, while the normal abort after a tool step keeps that Run open for its results. Debug logs distinguish checkpoint-envelope bytes, reachable blob bytes, seed size, and encoded Run-request estimate; raw blob bytes are never presented as tokens.
- **Edit rows can appear before the call is complete** — an announced edit opens a host tool row while Cursor streams its arguments. The eventual exec binds that row; if no call arrives, the provider closes it without asking the host to execute incomplete arguments ([early rows](src/early-tool-rows.ts)): with Cursor's own result when Cursor finished the edit itself (such as a string it could not find), as a completed note when another call ran first and this one comes later, and as failed only when the Run ended without it. A refused exec fails the row with the refusal reason, including when another call follows in the same step and when Cursor later reports a different completion. This includes `turn_ended` while other host tool results remain pending. An edit Cursor fails after reading the file shows as a failed row with Cursor's error even when no early row was open. Failure labels use the permitted catalog without reading target files. An edit whose file read must first go through OpenCode's `read` (any existing file) opens no early row: that read is the call's first exec and would close the row as a failed edit. When the call runs as a host tool the row did not predict (a rewrite with unchanged content stays a `write`, and a binary write is staged as the image save tool), the row completes with a note naming that call; OpenCode 2.x does not allow a started row to change its tool name.
- **Large uploads share a connection without the default 10 MB bottleneck** — direct and proxied Run connections use a 256 MB session-memory limit. This prevents queued sibling requests, or one large Node upload on a slow uplink, from triggering the default `NGHTTP2_ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` refusal. The limit remains finite. Cached connections hold the process alive only while a Run or health-check ping is active, so an idle connection does not prevent a headless process from exiting ([transport](src/transport/connect.ts)).
- **A quiet model or a running tool is still active** — every inbound frame, including heartbeats while a model composes tool arguments, renews Run liveness. Pending host execs receive client heartbeats; while tools run, the provider continues answering Cursor's KV requests and exec aborts. Open permission/question prompts and active descendant tools renew held Runs; a running tool can extend its lease up to four hours from its own start ([Run reader and heartbeats](src/language-model.ts), [leases](src/session.ts), [activity](src/activity.ts)).
- **Requests not yet checkpointed survive failed turns** — the next turn on the same checkpoint carries the missing request, including after a restart. Repeated retries do not stack copies of the same interruption note. A newer checkpoint, host Stop or rebuild from host history clears that carryover ([request tracking](src/lost-request.ts)).
- **Interrupted Runs resume from checkpoints** — a remote EOF, Connect end-stream, or trailer error is never emitted as a successful `stop`. When the failed Run produced an eligible checkpoint, the provider opens a new RPC for the same conversation and sends that state with `ResumeAction`, so completed text and tool work are not replayed. Before any stateful output, an interruption without a checkpoint can still rebase from OpenCode history. Stateful interruptions without a checkpoint are surfaced because replay would be ambiguous; retry exhaustion remains explicit. A transport closure after `turn_ended` is treated as successful completion.
- **Large reads are capped by OpenCode, and the cap is reported** — OpenCode 1.x `read` stops at `MAX_BYTES = 50 * 1024` and appends `(Output capped at 50 KB. Showing lines X-Y. Use offset=N to continue.)`. OpenCode 2.x prints `Read file <path>, lines <start>-<end>` with `N: ` prefixes and, when the page ends before EOF, `[Output truncated. Continue reading with offset: N]` (50 KB or 2,000 lines); it also shortens each individual line after 2,000 characters. The provider strips either envelope before returning content to Cursor so the model cannot echo wrappers into a later write, but it re-states every partial result: a native read appends a `[Partial read: …]` marker after the content, an MCP read gets a separate notice content item, and a Pi read carries structured `PiReadExecSuccess.truncation`. Relative grep, glob, and directory entries are resolved against the workspace root. Shell stdout reaches Cursor verbatim, including whitespace around internal wrapper markers; failed streams retain partial output. Successful timeout-shaped stdout remains text. Checkpointed turns, which do not resend the system prompt, get that same root on the user message. The structured `truncated` flag alone is not enough — verified against live `gpt-5.4-mini` and `grok-4.5` sessions, both of which asserted "highly confident" that partial content was the whole file until the textual marker was added. Deliberately paged reads (explicit `offset`/`limit`) are not marked unless the host also hits the byte cap or character-truncates a line. Whole-file writes and overwriting `Add File` patches that echo the marker are rejected before OpenCode executes them; targeted edits remain possible, including edits to source that quotes the warning text. Cursor's private legacy-edit read is handled separately as described above, so an edit can operate on a workspace file larger than 50 KB without turning the capped preview into a replacement. The cap is hardcoded in OpenCode's read tool — it is not the configurable `tool_output.max_bytes`, which governs `Truncate.Service` and not read's line accumulation — so ordinary model reads still require paging with `offset`.
- **No fallback models** — if Cursor’s `AvailableModels` API is unreachable and there is no local cache, the provider exposes no models.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth)
[![CI](https://github.com/anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth?style=social)](https://github.com/anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth)

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) authentication plugin that enables seamless interaction with the Antigravity CLI (`agy`) by hooking into its authentication, quota retrieval, and dynamic model fetching layers.

## Features

- **OAuth 2.0 Integration**: Uses Antigravity's OAuth flows for authentication.
- **Dynamic Model Retrieval**: Fetches available models based on user tier and current allocations.
- **Quota Tracking**: Injects the `agy_quota` tool into OpenCode to check usage limits directly.
- **Traffic Simulation**: Maintains background heartbeat with `agy` servers.
- **Dual OpenCode Compatibility**: Natively supports both OpenCode v1 (>= 1.18.29) and OpenCode v2 out of the box without breaking changes.

## Installation

Install the plugin from npm (or directly using local file configurations if developing):

```bash
npm install @anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth
```

## Configuration

Update your OpenCode configuration file (typically `opencode.json` at the root of your project or globally at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) to register the plugin and specify your Google Cloud Project ID.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth"],
  "provider": {
    "google-agy": {
      "options": {
        "projectId": "your-google-cloud-project-id"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

By default, the plugin registers a specialized provider ID to interface with `agy`.
You can switch your active OpenCode provider to `agy` or let the plugin inject authentication into your existing sessions.

### Environment Variables

If you are running OpenCode in environments with specific requirements for Antigravity, you can use the following environment variables:

- `OPENCODE_AGY_PROJECT_ID`: Specify your Google Cloud Project ID manually.
- `OPENCODE_AGY_AUTH_PROXY`: Define a proxy if accessing authentication endpoints behind a corporate firewall.
- `OPENCODE_AGY_ENDPOINT`: Override the default internal `daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com` API endpoint.
- `OPENCODE_AGY_VERBOSE_LOGS`: Set to `"1"` to enable verbose diagnostic logs for API calls and responses.

## Usage

Once installed and configured, OpenCode will automatically authenticate against Antigravity CLI when interacting with eligible models. If no active session exists, you will be prompted to complete an OAuth login.

Additionally, you can check your quota using slash commands directly in your OpenCode prompt:

- `/agyquota` - Per-model detail view. Shows remaining tokens, progress bars, and reset timers for every model variant. Use when you need the full breakdown of individual buckets.
- `/agyquotasummary` - High-level grouped view. Shows weekly and 5-hour limits aggregated by model family. Use when you want a quick overview of your allowance across all models.

You can also ask naturally:
> "What is my current agy quota?"
> "Show me my quota summary"

### Companion Plugin: `opencode-quota`

This repository is compatible with [`opencode-quota`](https://github.com/slkiser/opencode-quota), an OpenCode plugin for displaying quota information directly in your status bar or interface.

Follow the [Google AGY Quick Setup Guide](https://github.com/slkiser/opencode-quota/blob/main/docs/readme/providers.md#google-agy-quick-setup) to set them up together.

To use both plugins side by side, register them in your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": [
    "@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth",
    "opencode-quota"
  ],
  "provider": {
    "google-agy": {
      "options": {
        "projectId": "your-google-cloud-project-id"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

When used together, `opencode-quota` seamlessly visualizes rate limits and quotas for models authenticated through `google-agy`.

### Disk Persistence

The plugin persists turn-state and retry-cooldown data to disk so that it survives OpenCode restarts. Files are stored under `~/.config/opencode/` (or `%APPDATA%\opencode\` on Windows):

- `antigravity-turn-states.json` - tracks thinking/reasoning state across request turns, with a 24-hour TTL and 5-second throttled writes using atomic tmp+rename.
- Retry cooldowns are persisted via `CooldownStore` with the same atomic-write pattern.

Both stores initialize lazily at runtime - no filesystem reads occur at import time.

#### `diskEnabled` Parameter

`TurnStateTracker` accepts a `diskEnabled` constructor parameter (defaults to `true`):

```ts
import { TurnStateTracker } from "@anthonyhaussman/opencode-agy-auth/sdk/request/turn-state-tracker";

// Disk persistence enabled (default)
const tracker = new TurnStateTracker(true);

// Memory-only mode - no filesystem reads or writes
const tracker = new TurnStateTracker(false);
```

When `diskEnabled` is `false`, the tracker operates entirely in memory. All state is lost when the process exits. This is useful in restricted environments (containers, read-only filesystems) where disk access is unavailable or undesirable.

If disk initialization fails at runtime (permission error, corrupt file, etc.), the plugin automatically falls back to memory-only mode and logs a warning. No configuration is needed for normal use - disk persistence works out of the box.

> Policy discussion: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/discussions/22970

**Authenticate the Opencode CLI with an eligible organization-backed Google
account.** Gemini CLI OAuth is now limited to Gemini Code Assist Standard and
Enterprise subscriptions. Personal plans and the free tier must use the native
Gemini API-key flow instead of this plugin.

## Prerequisites

- [Opencode CLI](https://opencode.ai) installed.
- A Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise subscription. Consumer Google
  accounts are no longer supported by this OAuth flow.

## Installation

Add the plugin to your OpenCode configuration file
(`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or similar).

OpenCode V1:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-gemini-auth@latest"]
}
```

OpenCode V2:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-gemini-auth@latest"]
}
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Explicitly configure a Google Cloud `projectId` if you're using an
> organization-backed Gemini Code Assist subscription
> (`Standard`/`Enterprise`) or a company, school, or Google Workspace account.
> Most individual Google accounts should not need this. `Google AI Plus` is not
> a Gemini Code Assist subscription tier. You can still set `projectId` to
> force a specific project.

### OpenCode V2 Compatibility

OpenCode V2 loads the package's native `./server` entrypoint. It registers the
Gemini CLI OAuth method through `integration.transform` and rewrites Google
provider requests and responses through provider-scoped V2 session HTTP hooks.
The entrypoint targets OpenCode 2.0.14 and uses `Plugin.define` from
`@opencode/plugin@2.0.14`. Project settings are read through `ctx.provider.get`.
Provider lookup failures are reported instead of silently selecting another
Google Cloud project.

The V1 entrypoint remains unchanged. The V2 entrypoint currently covers login
and model requests; the `/gquota` command, quota tool, retry transport, and TUI
capacity notifications remain V1-only.

## Usage

1. **Login**: Run `opencode auth login` on V1 or open `/connect` in OpenCode V2.

2. **Select Provider**: Choose **Google** from the list.
3. **Authenticate**: Select **OAuth with Google (Gemini CLI)**.
   - A browser window will open for you to approve the access.
   - The plugin spins up a temporary local server to capture the callback.
   - If the local server fails (e.g., port in use or headless environment),
     you can manually paste the callback URL or just the authorization code.

Once authenticated, Opencode will use your Google account for Gemini requests.

On V1, check your current Gemini Code Assist quota buckets with:

```bash
/gquota
```

## Configuration

### Google Cloud Project

By default, the plugin attempts to provision or find a suitable Google Cloud
project. To force a specific project, set the `projectId` in your configuration
or via environment variables:

OpenCode V1:

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "google": {
      "options": {
        "projectId": "your-specific-project-id"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

OpenCode V2:

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "google": {
      "settings": {
        "projectId": "your-specific-project-id"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

You can also set `OPENCODE_GEMINI_PROJECT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, or
`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` to supply the project ID via environment variables.

In V2, `OPENCODE_GEMINI_PROJECT_ID` overrides the configured project. The
generic Google variables are fallbacks used only when the provider has no
configured project, with `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` before `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`.

### Proxy

If your network requires an HTTP proxy for Google API calls, set
`OPENCODE_GEMINI_AUTH_PROXY` before starting Opencode:

```bash
OPENCODE_GEMINI_AUTH_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8080 opencode
```

This is passed to Bun's `fetch` proxy option and applies to OAuth, token
refresh, project/quota lookup, and Gemini request forwarding.

### Model list

If you want to remove unusable models from the picker, use OpenCode's
`provider.google.whitelist` or `provider.google.blacklist` settings.

- `whitelist`: only show the listed model IDs.
- `blacklist`: hide specific model IDs from the default list.
- `models`: define or override model metadata/options, but does not remove the
  default models by itself.

Use the exact model IDs reported by `opencode models google` when building these
lists.

Example: keep only a small Gemini model list visible.

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "google": {
      "whitelist": [
        "gemini-2.5-flash",
        "gemini-2.5-pro",
        "gemini-3-flash-preview",
        "gemini-3-pro-preview"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Example: hide a few unwanted defaults while keeping the rest.

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "google": {
      "blacklist": [
        "gemini-2.0-flash-exp",
        "gemini-1.5-pro"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Below are example model entries you can add under `provider.google.models` in your
Opencode config. Each model can include an `options.thinkingConfig` block to
enable "thinking" features.

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "google": {
      "models": {
        "gemini-2.5-flash": {
          "options": {
            "thinkingConfig": {
              "thinkingBudget": 8192,
              "includeThoughts": true
            }
          }
        },
        "gemini-2.5-pro": {
          "options": {
            "thinkingConfig": {
              "thinkingBudget": 8192,
              "includeThoughts": true
            }
          }
        },
        "gemini-3-flash-preview": {
          "options": {
            "thinkingConfig": {
              "thinkingLevel": "high",
              "includeThoughts": true
            }
          }
        },
        "gemini-3-pro-preview": {
          "options": {
            "thinkingConfig": {
              "thinkingLevel": "high",
              "includeThoughts": true
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Note: Available model names and previews may change—check Google's documentation or
the Gemini product page for the current model identifiers.

### Thinking Models

The plugin supports configuring Gemini "thinking" features per-model via
`thinkingConfig`. The available fields depend on the model family:

- For Gemini 3 models: use `thinkingLevel` with values `"low"` or `"high"`.
- For Gemini 2.5 models: use `thinkingBudget` (token count).
- `includeThoughts` (boolean) controls whether the model emits internal thoughts.

A combined example showing both model types:

```json
{
  "provider": {
    "google": {
      "models": {
        "gemini-3-pro-preview": {
          "options": {
            "thinkingConfig": {
              "thinkingLevel": "high",
              "includeThoughts": true
            }
          }
        },
        "gemini-2.5-flash": {
          "options": {
            "thinkingConfig": {
              "thinkingBudget": 8192,
              "includeThoughts": true
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

If you don't set a `thinkingConfig` for a model, the plugin will use default
behavior for that model.

The plugin also accepts request payloads that put `thinkingConfig` at the root
and normalizes them into `generationConfig.thinkingConfig` before forwarding to
Gemini Code Assist.

## Troubleshooting

### Manual Google Cloud Setup

If automatic provisioning fails, you may need to set up the project manually:

1. Go to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. Create or select a project.
3. Enable the **Gemini for Google Cloud API**
   (`cloudaicompanion.googleapis.com`).
4. Configure the `projectId` in your Opencode config as shown above.

### Quotas, Plans, and 429 Errors

Common causes of `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` or `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED`:

- **No project ID configured**: the plugin uses a managed free-tier project, which has lower quotas.
- **Model-specific limits**: quotas are tracked per model (e.g., `gemini-3-pro-preview` vs `gemini-3-flash-preview`).
- **Large prompts**: OAuth/Code Assist does not support cached content, so long system prompts and history can burn quota quickly.
- **Parallel sessions**: multiple Opencode windows can drain the same bucket.

Notes:

- **Gemini CLI auto-fallbacks**: the official CLI may fall back to Flash when Pro quotas are exhausted, so it can appear to “work” even if the Pro bucket is depleted.
- **Org-backed Code Assist subscriptions require a project**: if you're using Gemini Code Assist `Standard` or `Enterprise`, set `provider.google.options.projectId` (or `OPENCODE_GEMINI_PROJECT_ID`) and re-authenticate.

### Debugging

To view detailed logs of Gemini requests and responses, set the
`OPENCODE_GEMINI_DEBUG` environment variable:

```bash
OPENCODE_GEMINI_DEBUG=1 opencode
```

This will generate `gemini-debug-<timestamp>.log` files in your working
directory containing sanitized request/response details.

This plugin mirrors the official Gemini CLI OAuth flow and Code Assist
endpoints. In particular, project onboarding and quota retry handling follow

# Contributing to opencode-quota

Thanks for contributing! Please read this before you open an issue or PR.

## Issues first

- Open an issue before a feature, fix, refactor, or behavior change. Opening the issue and PR together is fine.
- Link it in the PR with `Fixes #<issue>` or `Refs #<issue>`. A PR that changes a default setting or the UI (the TUI, the Desktop GUI) needs a linked issue first; without one it gets the `needs info` label. For anything else without an issue, explain the reason and scope in the PR.
- Use an issue form (bug, feature, or provider request). Write a short title that names the problem you see, not the fix; the form adds the label, so skip `[bug]`-style prefixes.
- An issue opened without a form gets the `needs info` label and a request to open a new one with a form.
- Very short or mostly empty issues get the `needs info` label. Adding the details removes it. `needs info` issues close after 21 days without activity; nothing else auto-closes.

## If an AI writes your issue or PR

Paste this to your AI first:

> Start with what a user sees on screen. Make the title the problem, not the fix. Keep it under 15 lines. Name no function, file or commit unless asked. Fill in every field of the issue form. Test on a released OpenCode version first. A PR that changes a default or the UI needs a linked issue first.

## Setup

Node.js 22.22.1+, 24.11+ or 26+ (what Vite+ and its staged-file check need; the published plugin itself runs on `^22.13.0 || >=23.4.0`), Git 2.32+ and pnpm 11:

```sh
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@11.28.9 --activate
pnpm install
```

`pnpm install` also sets up the Git hooks with Vite+ (`vp config`): pre-commit runs `vp staged`, which formats and lints the staged files, fixes what it can and stages the fixes (rules in the `staged` block of `vite.config.ts`); pre-push runs `pnpm verify`. The hook scripts are in `.github/hooks/`. Each checkout and Git worktree runs its own copy, so run `pnpm install` in each one.

If Git's `core.hooksPath` already points to another folder, `pnpm install` leaves it alone and prints `core.hooksPath is already set to "…", skipping`, and these hooks don't run. `pnpm exec vp hooks status --hooks-dir .github/hooks` shows the current state. To skip the hooks for one command, set `VP_GIT_HOOKS=0`.

### Activate hooks in a clone that uses Lefthook

`core.hooksPath` is Git's setting for the folder containing hook programs. Linked worktrees normally share this setting. Check its source and value from the repository folder:

```sh
git config --show-origin --get-all core.hooksPath
```

If the setting comes from this repository's `.git/config` and points to its Lefthook hook folder, remove that setting and activate Vite+ from a v6 checkout:

```sh
git config --local --unset-all core.hooksPath
pnpm install
pnpm exec vp hooks enable --hooks-dir .github/hooks
pnpm exec vp hooks status --hooks-dir .github/hooks
```

The status must show `core.hooksPath` as `.github/hooks/_`, an installed dispatcher, and the `pre-commit` and `pre-push` scripts. A skipped installation does not activate these checks. If the setting belongs to another hook system or comes from global or worktree-specific configuration, keep it and resolve that setup before using these instructions.

### Working on both v4 and v6

v4 and v6 both use Vite+. With the relative `.github/hooks/_` setting, each worktree needs its own installed hook programs. Run `pnpm install` in every existing worktree after activating this setting, and after switching a checkout between v4 and v6. Install dependencies before committing or pushing from a new worktree.

Git's `info/exclude` file lists local files to ignore and is shared by linked worktrees. Add the generated hook folder there once per clone so v4's installed hooks cannot be accidentally staged:

```sh
printf '\n/.github/hooks/_/\n' >> "$(git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude)"
```

## Checks

Run `pnpm verify` before opening a PR. It runs lint and formatting, the TypeScript-version and history checks, the build (its `tsc` step is the type check), all tests (the cross-surface test among them), and the package contents check. CI runs the same command on Linux and only the build, tests and package contents check (`pnpm run verify:platform`) on Windows. A smoke job then installs the packed package on Node 22 and 24 as a smoke test, once into a project and once globally with npm 12.

For quick iteration: `pnpm run test:watch`.

## Rules the code must keep

- **No AI calls.** Never send a request to an AI model to produce anything the plugin shows (quota rows, toasts, command output); it would spend the user's tokens. Calling a provider's quota or billing API is fine.
- **OpenCode 2 only.** No OpenCode 1 code, APIs, or tables.
- **Server vs. TUI.** The server plugin (`src/plugin.ts`) reads providers, settings, and OpenCode's history, and registers the slash commands, the agent tools, and the `slkiser.opencode-quota` RPC. The TUI plugin (`src/tui/index.tsx`) and the experimental GUI plugin for Desktop (`src/gui/index.tsx`; OpenCode Web shows no plugin GUI, the `./gui-experimental` export) only draw what the RPC returns and never import provider or credential code.
- **One status report.** `/quota_status`, the `quota_status` tool, and the RPC `status` method go through `buildQuotaDialogCommandOutput()`; `opencode-quota status` uses `buildStatusReportData()`, which that function wraps. Every value the report prints comes from a known list, a formatted number, or a placeholder (`tests/lib.quota-status.test.ts` checks this).
- **Credentials.** Read OpenCode logins only through `ctx.integration` in `src/lib/opencode-auth.ts`. The only exception is the terminal command (`src/lib/cli-show.ts`), which uses `src/lib/opencode-auth-sqlite.ts`; the plugins must never reach that file.
- **Money.** Use the shared formatter, which shows USD as `$12.50` and other currencies with an ISO code after the amount, such as `8.25 CNY`. Never convert amounts or add up different currencies.
- Keep these boundary tests passing and up to date: `tests/plugin.command-handled-boundary.test.ts`, `tests/tui-dist-import-graph.test.ts`, `tests/quota-provider-boundary.test.ts`, `tests/v6-cross-surface.test.ts`.

## Provider changes

**Built-in providers** are considered only when:

- the provider is on [models.dev](https://models.dev/),
- at least two independent users asked for it (your own request, repeat comments, and requests from the provider's own company don't count),
- it has a documented API (no login cookies or website scraping), and
- the PR links that evidence and explains why a custom provider isn't enough.

Even then, it needs a reasonable maintenance cost.

**Pick the right path:**

| You want to… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Use an OpenAI-compatible model service OpenCode doesn't include | an OpenCode custom provider |
| Track quota for a provider OpenCode already exposes (request estimates or one fixed quota endpoint) | an OpenCode Quota custom provider ([ask your agent](../docs/readme/providers.md#custom-providers)); its `providerId` must match OpenCode's |
| Anything the custom path can't do, and the policy above is met | a built-in provider |

**Building one:** for API-key or token providers, start from `.github/provider-template/` (see its README), replace every example name, and add tests for every auth source. Use the setup label in `docs/readme/providers.md` that matches reality: `Automatic` or `Needs setup`.

**Every row** follows the row contract in `src/providers/contract.ts`. Pick `type` by what the number means (`quota`, `budget`, `usage`, `balance`, `status`), not by what's easiest to draw; `method` by how it was read (`remote_api`, `dashboard_scrape`, `local_cli`, `local_estimation`); and `authority` by who worked it out (`provider_reported` or `locally_derived`). A row's `key` is part of its id, which users' settings use, so it never changes once released.

Rich providers (more than a percentage) also:

- send numbers as typed `used`, `limit`, `remaining` or `amount` values and yes/no as `flag`; never pre-formatted money strings;
- set an explicit `primary` or `supplementary` prominence;
- keep `used`, `limit`, and `remaining` literal;
- keep labels short: the concept only, no values, units, or reset text.

A simple percentage-only provider may keep the plain percent row (`quotaRow`).

# Configuration

Most people need no settings. To change one, open `/quota_settings` in the TUI: every setting is a line there, with its values. In OpenCode Desktop (`2.2.0+`, experimental), the Quota page in OpenCode's settings edits the same file.

## Where settings live

One global file, `settings.jsonc`:

- `~/.config/opencode/opencode-quota/settings.jsonc` on every OS (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/...` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set)
- `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/opencode-quota/settings.jsonc` when `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` is set (it replaces the global folder, like OpenCode 2)

There are no project settings. Comments and trailing commas are allowed. Every key is optional; a missing or invalid value uses its default. `/quota_status` shows the file it reads and any problems in it.

The file holds only the settings you change, so the rest follow their defaults, also when a newer version changes one. Without the file nothing is written; the first Save, Plugin tab switch or agent change creates it. Settings from 4.x or 5.x convert on the first start: see [Updating](updating.md#moving-from-5x).

The TUI quota window's tabs are Usage, Limits, Plugin, then the Settings tabs **Layout** (**All places**, then a page each for Sidebar, Collapsed, Status line and Toast), **Colors** and **Providers**. `/quota_usage`, `/quota`, `/quota_status` and `/quota_settings` open it on Usage, Limits, Plugin and Layout. While you edit, the sidebar, status line, toasts and quota window show your unsaved changes. **Save** writes them and keeps the file's comments, **Discard** drops them, and **Reset page** (**Reset tab** on Colors and Providers) puts that page back to its defaults on Save, except row names. The **Plugin** tab (`/quota_status`) has the **Old command names**, **Quota file (JSON)** and **OpenTelemetry metrics** switches, which save as soon as you change them. A file edit or a Save reaches every open TUI within a few seconds.

Three settings are file only: `providers.custom` ([custom providers](providers.md#custom-providers)), `providers.anthropic.binaryPath` and `system.exportPath`. Credentials never go in this file: see [API keys](providers.md#api-keys).

Nest the keys in the file:

```jsonc
{
  "sidebar": { "sessionTokens": false },
  "collapsed": { "window": { "anthropic": "five_hour" } },
  "statusLine": { "window": { "anthropic": "week" } },
  "toast": { "afterReply": "off" },
  "colors": { "good": "green" },
  "layout": { "barWidth": 10 },
  "words": { "percent": "used", "reset": "compact" },
  "providers": { "off": ["openai"], "checking": { "requestTimeoutMs": 12000 } },
  "system": { "exportFile": true },
}
```

## TUI surfaces

- **Sidebar:** the `Quota` panel in a session's sidebar. Click its title to collapse it to one line per provider (**Collapsed**).
- **Status line:** under the message box when no sidebar panel with quota is on screen. **Next to the sidebar** on its page shows it there too.
- **Toasts:** after compaction, when every provider fails, and after a reply once a shown limit is getting low.

OpenCode Desktop (`2.2.0+`, experimental) shows the same settings in its own places: `sidebar` in a pinned Quota side tab, `collapsed` in a titlebar pill (and in the Quota side tab when folded), `statusLine` in a strip at the bottom of the window and a pill above the message box (the strip also shows while the Quota tab does; `statusLine.withSidePanel: false` hides it then; `statusLine.composerPill: false` hides only the pill), and `toast` in its toasts, with the Quota side tab's rows and bars (`toast.layout` doesn't apply there; a reset notice is a sentence). Web has none of these; there `/quota`, `/quota_usage` and `/quota_status` post a report in the chat.

Read an export file For a status bar or another tool that checks quota often. tmux and Starship examples tmux config: ```bash set -g status-interval 30 set -g status-right '#(jq -r "[.providers|to_entries[]|select(.value.status==\"ok\")|first(.value.entries[]?|select(.renderType==\"percent\" and .percentRemaining!=null))|(.percentRemaining|floor|tostring)+\"%\"]|join(\" | \")" ~/.cache/opencode/quota-export.json 2>/dev/null)' ``` `starship.toml`: ```toml [custom.quota] command = "jq -r '[.providers|to_entries[]|select(.value.status==\"ok\")|first(.value.entries[]?|select(.renderType==\"percent\" and .percentRemaining!=null))|(.percentRemaining|floor|tostring)+\"%\"]|join(\" \")' ~/.cache/opencode/quota-export.json 2>/dev/null" when = "true" interval = 60 ```
## 3. Send OpenTelemetry metrics Only when OpenCode's server process (normally the background service) already has an OpenTelemetry metrics provider and exporter; OpenCode Quota does not create or configure them. Turn on **OpenTelemetry metrics** on the Plugin tab (`/quota_status`), or add this to `opencode-quota/settings.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "system": { "telemetry": true } } ``` OpenCode Quota then publishes two gauges from the results already in memory, with no refresh loop of its own. Without a global metrics provider, nothing is sent. | Metric | Meaning | Labels | | --- | --- | --- | | `opencode.quota.consumed` | Used quota from `0` to `1` | `quota.provider`, `quota.result_type`, `quota.window` | | `opencode.quota.cache.age` | Age of cached data in seconds | `quota.provider` |
Metric values and privacy `opencode.quota.consumed` uses percentage rows only: `(100 - percentRemaining) / 100`, limited to `0` to `1`. Rows without a percentage feed neither gauge. - `quota.provider` is a maintained provider ID, `custom`, or `other`. - `quota.result_type` is `quota` (rate limits too), `usage` (spending too), `budget`, `balance`, or `status`. - `quota.window` is `rpm`, `hour`, `five_hour`, `session`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`, `mcp`, `code_review`, or `unknown`. When several rows map to the same labels, OpenCode Quota reports the highest consumed ratio or oldest cache age. Display names, account IDs, configured source IDs, credentials, URLs, paths, errors, and raw responses are never labels.
## JSON basics The command and export file both use JSON schema version `3`. Every provider has a `status`, and the other fields depend on it: | Status | Meaning | Fields | | --- | --- | --- | | `ok` | Data is available | `fetchedAt`, `entries` | | `partial` | Some data worked and some failed | `fetchedAt`, `entries`, `errors` | | `error` | The provider failed | `fetchedAt`, a safe `error` message | | `unavailable` | Not set up, or no saved data | none required | Treat `status: "partial"` as incomplete. A provider's `error` (and each `errors` message) is the short text the TUI shows, for example `Sign in again` or `Provider error 503`. `show --json` writes the quota OpenCode saved last; the export file writes each provider's last check, a failed one too. A percentage entry has `renderType: "percent"` and `percentRemaining`. A value entry has `renderType: "value"` and `value`: the text the TUI shows (for example `$12.50 left` or `$2.50/$10.00`), or `Enabled` / `Disabled` for a yes/no row. A provider can have several rows of both kinds, so select by `renderType` and `resultType`, never by position. The `words` settings never change JSON, threshold checks use percentage rows only, and version 3 has no row prominence or separate used, limit, and remaining amounts. Every entry has these fields: | Field | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `id` | The row's stable id, `provider.key` (for example `copilot.allowance`), the same id the TUI's hide, rename and order settings use. The rows of two accounts of one provider share it; `account` tells them apart. | | `name` | `Provider (account) Label`, for example `Copilot (pro) Premium requests` | | `resultType` | `quota` (rate limits too), `usage` (spending too), `budget`, `balance`, or `status` | | `acquisitionMethod` | `remote_api`, `dashboard_scrape`, `local_cli`, or `local_estimation` | | `ownership` | `maintained`, or `user_configured` for rows from `providers.custom` | | `authority` | `provider_reported` or `locally_derived` | Optional entry fields are `account` (the account the TUI shows, for example `pro`; two logins with the same account get `pro` and `pro 2`), `window` (for example `5h`, `Weekly`, `Monthly`) and `resetAt` (Unix seconds). Secrets, credentials, URLs, checked paths, and raw provider responses remain excluded from public JSON. Use `/quota_status` for live diagnostics. Rows from a `providers.custom` definition appear under `providers["quota-providers"]`, each with the id `quota-providers.custom..`. After a check, that provider's `sources` lists every definition except the built-in tunings, in file order, each with exactly `id`, `providerId`, `status` (`ok`, `error` or `unavailable`) and `entryCount`. A switched-off definition has `"enabled": false` instead of a `status`, and `entryCount` `0`. A definition can be `ok` while failed mapping candidates make the provider `partial`.
Small JSON example ```json { "version": 3, "exportedAt": 1748736000, "fromCache": true, "cacheAgeSeconds": 42, "providers": { "copilot": { "status": "ok", "fetchedAt": 1748735958, "entries": [ { "id": "copilot.allowance", "name": "Copilot (pro) Premium requests", "account": "pro", "resultType": "quota", "acquisitionMethod": "remote_api", "ownership": "maintained", "authority": "provider_reported", "renderType": "percent", "percentRemaining": 62.3 } ] } } } ```

## Custom providers Providers OpenCode Quota doesn't include (for example Chutes AI, NanoGPT, Synthetic, Kilo Gateway) can be added as a custom provider, read from the provider's quota API (`remote-api`) or estimated by counting OpenCode's requests (`local-estimate`). Ask your agent to add a custom provider: paste this into OpenCode and replace ``: ```text Add a custom OpenCode Quota provider for with the quota_provider_add tool, following docs/readme/providers.md#custom-providers in https://github.com/slkiser/opencode-quota. Never put a key or other secret in the definition: set apiKeyEnv to the name of the environment variable that holds the key, or leave it out to use the key OpenCode has for that provider. The tool saves the provider switched off; tell me the address and key source it returns. After I switch it on, test it with quota_provider_test, and fix what it reports (add it again with the same id; I switch it on again) until it shows rows. ``` The agent saves the provider switched off: until you switch it on, it is never fetched and its key is never sent, and no agent tool can switch it on. Switch it on by setting `"enabled": true` in `opencode-quota/settings.jsonc`, or tick it in `/quota_settings` → **Providers**, which shows its address and the key it sends. The agent tools change only OpenCode Quota's own settings file, never `opencode.json`, and refuse a definition holding anything that looks like a key. To write one yourself, add it to `providers.custom` in `settings.jsonc` ([where](configuration.md#where-settings-live)); `/quota_status` checks it with the plugin's own validator. - **Identity:** `id` is the stable identity; add `providerId` only when it differs. A definition is on unless it has `"enabled": false`. Definitions keep file order, and `custom` in `providers.off` skips them all. - **Credentials:** the variable named by `apiKeyEnv`, then `provider..options.apiKey` in the [OpenCode config files](troubleshooting.md#opencode-config-files) (no `{env:…}` unless it names `apiKeyEnv`), then an API-key login saved in OpenCode 2 (`opencode.db`) for that provider id. - **Models:** `modelIds` only limits `words.onlyCurrentModel` and which requests a local estimate counts. Use exact, case-sensitive model ids without the provider prefix, or leave it out to cover every model of that provider. - **Check interval:** optional `minIntervalMs` is a positive whole number of milliseconds between automatic checks of this definition in each running OpenCode (for example `600000` for ten minutes); skipped checks keep the last rows and error. Manual refresh and `/quota_status` check immediately. - **Local estimate:** 1–16 windows; `utc-day` resets at UTC midnight, `rolling` uses `durationMinutes` (up to 366 days). Every window needs `requestLimit`; `usdBudget` is optional. Each check counts the completed requests in OpenCode's own messages; nothing else is stored. - **Local estimate prices:** the automatic match comes first (models.dev, and Cursor's own prices for Auto, Composer and Grok); `pricingModelMap` is used only where it finds none and cannot override a successful automatic match. If any request cannot be priced, the request counts stay and the budget percentage is reported unavailable. - **Not accepted:** scripts, methods, custom headers, templates, executable mappings, regular expressions, JSONPath, and automatic endpoint discovery. - A custom model provider still needs its normal OpenCode provider/model config. `/connect` → **Other** stores its credential, not its model setup. - OpenRouter is built in; a custom OpenRouter definition only helps for a different endpoint or label. Alibaba Token Plan uses the reserved `alibaba-token-plan` id and stays a separate official-CLI provider; `alibaba-token-plan-cn` is another name for the same CLI.

Remote API response rules `mode: "remote-api"` accepts three formats: - `quota-v1` reads the standard OpenCode Quota envelope. - `json-v1` maps fields from a strict JSON response through a declarative adapter. - `openrouter-key-v1` reads OpenRouter's key response, with the same rows as the [built-in OpenRouter](#openrouter). A `quota-v1` response looks like this: ```json { "version": "quota-v1", "entries": [ { "kind": "percent", "name": "Requests", "resultType": "quota", "percentRemaining": 42, "label": "Daily:" }, { "kind": "value", "name": "Spend", "resultType": "spend", "value": "$12.50" } ] } ``` A `json-v1` adapter is built from literal property segments, compatible metric sources, and optional units and timestamps. This example maps `remaining`, `limit`, and `status` from one response object: ```json { "mappings": [ { "resultType": "quota", "name": "Requests", "label": "Daily:", "unit": "requests", "unitPosition": "suffix", "metric": { "type": "remaining-limit", "remaining": { "path": ["remaining"] }, "limit": { "path": ["limit"] } } }, { "resultType": "status", "name": "Status", "metric": { "type": "status", "value": { "path": ["status"] } } } ] } ``` Adapter rules: - **Rows:** optional `rowsPath` and 1–16 `mappings`. Without `rowsPath`, an object is one item and an array is a list of items; with it, the array it names is the list. A list holds 1–100 items, and each mapping makes one row per item. With more than one item, the rows are numbered `Daily 1`, `Daily 2`, …: item 1 keeps the plain row id and later items add `.2`, `.3`, …. - **Mapping names:** each name keys its rows, so names must still differ when spaces count as `_` (`Daily limit` and `Daily_limit` clash; `Daily-limit` is fine). - **Paths:** 1–8 literal own-property segments of 1–64 Unicode code points. Dots and brackets mean nothing special; array indexes and the segments `__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` are rejected. - **Size:** adapter input is limited to 8 container levels, 128 objects, 384 object properties, and 640 array eleme …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… pSeek Shows your account balance: one **Total balance** row per currency, never added up or converted (detailed output adds **Granted balance** and **Topped-up balance**), or the API's availability status when there is no valid balance. Both show which settings, providers, logins, and local files OpenCode Quota found. 2. Find the provider or feature that fails, and follow the matching fix below. 3. Restart OpenCode after changing `opencode.json`. Changes to logins and `settings.jsonc` apply without a restart. Every provider missing? Check that `@slkiser/opencode-quota` is in the `plugin` list of `opencode.jsonc` or `.json`. That one entry also loads the TUI; no `tui.json` entry is needed. ## Logins OpenCode Quota never reads OpenCode's `auth.json`. Inside OpenCode, it asks OpenCode 2 for logins (OpenCode keeps them in `opencode.db`). OpenCode 2 copies `auth.json` only once, the first time it starts. **If a provider is missing, log in to it again in OpenCode 2.** A login OpenCode could not return (for example after a failed token refresh) shows as an error row and under `credential_source` → `failures`; log in to that provider again. `/quota_status` also shows the `opencode.db` path used for session and token history. `OPENCODE_DB` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` change it. Custom or source builds of OpenCode may use `opencode-.db`; set `OPENCODE_DB` to that file's path. ## Service environment The TUI, Web, and Desktop get their numbers from OpenCode's background service. The service takes `PATH` and environment variables from whatever started it first, not from the terminal you use now, and it runs in your home folder. The terminal command uses your terminal's `PATH`, environment, and current folder instead. - **`claude` or `bl` not found, or an API-key variable ignored:** in a terminal where they work, run `opencode service restart`. To keep that `PATH` for every later start, run `opencode service set env PATH "$PATH"` (it stops the service; open OpenCode again). For Claude you can instead set `providers.anthropic.binaryPath`. - Cursor's plugin-entry check reads the [OpenCode config files](#opencode-config-files) of the session's folder, not of the service's folder. ## OpenCode config files OpenCode Quota reads OpenCode's own config files the way OpenCode does. For a session, these count, from lowest to highest rank: 1. `opencode.json`, then `opencode.jsonc`, in the global OpenCode folder (`$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`, else `~/.config/opencode`). 2. The file `OPENCODE_CONFIG` names. 3. `opencode.json`, then `opencode.jsonc`, in every folder from the top of the drive down to the session's folder. 4. The same two files in the `.opencode` folder of each of those folders, from the top down. A file ranked higher wins. Both kinds may hold comments and trailing commas. With `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG` (or `OPENCODE_CONFIG_PROJECT_DISABLE`) set to `1` or `true`, only 1 and 2 count. The terminal command uses the folder it runs in as the session's folder. `/quota_status` (the slash command and the `quota_status` tool; the Plugin tab never writes) adds an empty `provider.` entry for each available provider that none of these files declares, under a `// Detected authentication; …` comment in `opencode.jsonc`. It writes only the global folder's `opencode.jsonc`, else its `opencode.json`, else a new `opencode.jsonc`. It keeps comments, writes through a symlink, writes nothing when the file changed while it ran, and never writes a project file. ## Terminal commands `opencode-quota show` and `opencode-quota status` run in your terminal, not in OpenCode: - They work with OpenCode closed, read logins from `opencode.db` read-only, and read the same global `settings.jsonc` as OpenCode. - They never refresh a token, so a sign-in can show as expired (for example `Sign in again`) until you open OpenCode. - They use your shell's `PATH` and API-key variables. `status --json` prints the report as data: `version` (`"6"`), `generatedAt`, `config`, `providers`, `pricing`, and `liveProbes`. ## Common problems | Problem | Try this | | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Slash commands are missing | Check the plugin entry above, then restart OpenCode. | | `/quota` shows no providers | Run `/quota_status` and check provider detection and [logins](#logins). | | Sidebar is missing | Open a session: the `Quota` panel is in its sidebar. A collapsed panel opens when you click its title. | | No Quota GUI in OpenCode Desktop | It needs OpenCode `2.2.0+` and its switch on in **Settings → Extensions → Plugins**. Web shows no plugin GUI. | | Old `/quota` reports reach the AI after uninstalling | The plugin filtered them out while installed. Delete those messages or start a new chat. | | `/quota_usage` is empty | Start OpenCode once so it creates `opencode.db`, then use a model. | | Pricing looks old | Press `p` in the TUI's Usage tab (`/quota_usage`). | | Terminal shows a sign-in as expired but OpenCode shows data | The terminal never refreshes tokens. ### Added

### Changed

### Fixed

- Unwrapping host `<system-update>` notes now takes linear time, so a note with many unclosed `<system-update>` tags can no longer stall a turn (CodeQL `js/polynomial-redos`).
- Image bursts no longer lose pending saves at the ninth image. Accepted images retain their bytes through saving; a shared 400 MiB payload budget refuses only new writes that do not fit. Refused copies of attached images also notify the model, immediately or on the next user turn if Cursor has ended the Run ([#165](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/issues/165), [#166](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/pull/166), [@nkoynov](https://github.com/nkoynov)).
- New manual review payloads require a revision-matched evidence ledger and isolated-check exit record; preview and publication recheck retained evidence while preserving existing pending previews.
- Debug and recovery logs retain recent diagnostics with OpenCode-style in-place trimming by default, or configurable numbered archives with `CURSOR_PROVIDER_DEBUG_LOG_MODE=rotate` ([#160](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/issues/160), [@nkoynov](https://github.com/nkoynov)).
- Log rotation preserves archives when the active file cannot be renamed, and stale maintenance cleanup preserves replacement owners' locks ([#163](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/pull/163), [@nkoynov](https://github.com/nkoynov)).
- A Run Cursor cuts right after a tool result now rebuilds from host history when it earlier delivered an early steer or host note that history still holds, instead of ending the turn as "automatic retry unsafe" ([#159](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/issues/159), [@nkoynov](https://github.com/nkoynov)).
- That rebuild is no longer refused (`missing-host-results`) when Cursor earlier waited on a background shell: its polls of the shell's terminal record are answered by the provider, ran nothing on the host, and no longer count as tool calls without a result ([#159](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/issues/159), [@nkoynov](https://github.com/nkoynov)).
- The same rebuild also proceeds after the provider itself answered the empty read before a new file's edit or a Task attachment read, provided history holds that call's result, or a read of a missing file ([#172](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/issues/172), [@nkoynov](https://github.com/nkoynov)).
- A failed OpenCode 1.x download no longer leaves the previous binary in place and reports a successful install.
- OpenCode 1.x model metadata now sets `reasoning` from reasoning variants too, not only `supports_thinking`, covering `deepseek-v41-flash-1017`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5` and `muse-wonder-1.0` ([#168](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/issues/168), [#169](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/pull/169), [@adonm](https://github.com/adonm)).

- Review setup reports its read-only GitHub lookup accurately instead of claiming no GitHub call occurred ([#161](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/pull/161)).
- Manual reviews preserve failed command statuses and exit codes alongside evidence of baseline or environment failures; publication supports bundled GitHub CLIs without `--slurp` ([#161](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/pull/161)).
- Local test checks stop owned descendants before removing their source snapshot, including after a successful leader, SIGINT, SIGTERM, or repeated cancellation ([#161](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/pull/161)).
- Live OpenCode smoke tests remove native runtime scratch files on exit while preserving pre-existing files in the configured temp root.

# Security

## Threat Model

### Overview

cursor-opencode-provider is an OpenCode plugin and AI SDK provider that speaks Cursor's private agent protocol. Through the host it can trigger powerful tools (shell, file operations, network access via host MCP/tools) and it sends workspace context, instructions, and tool results to Cursor.

### No Sandbox

Neither this provider nor OpenCode's permission system is a security sandbox. Permissions help users review and control actions; they are not an isolation boundary.

If you need isolation, run the host in a disposable container, virtual machine, or similarly restricted environment. Review project instructions and third-party tool or MCP server configuration before allowing them to execute.

### Project `instructions` can include arbitrary local paths

This provider mirrors OpenCode's trust model for project configuration. That has implications for what ends up in Cursor context.

OpenCode's `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc` `instructions` array may list:

- relative paths / globs (e.g. `.cursor/rules/*.md`)
- absolute paths
- home-relative paths (`~/…`)
- remote URLs supported by the host

OpenCode owns instruction discovery and supplies the resulting system prompt
to the AI SDK provider. This package forwards that prompt as Cursor's
always-apply system-instructions rule; it does not independently read instruction
or skill file bodies or fetch instruction URLs. Its merged-config read supplies
MCP server ids, plugin metadata and interaction guidance
([`src/context/rules.ts`](src/context/rules.ts),
[`src/context/build.ts`](src/context/build.ts)).

So a project config like:

```json
{
  "instructions": ["docs/project-guide.md", "/absolute/path/to/approved-guide.md"]
}
```

can cause those files to be read by OpenCode and included in the prompt sent to
Cursor. The provider does not add an instruction-path allowlist or remove content
already supplied by the host. Review instruction paths before enabling project
configuration, especially if they could refer to sensitive local files.

Treat project `opencode.json` as **trusted**. Do not open untrusted repositories with project config enabled if that is unacceptable.

#### Mitigation: disable project config

To ignore project-level OpenCode config (including project `instructions` and project `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `CONTEXT.md` discovery), set:

```bash
export OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1
```

Set this before starting OpenCode and use the host's project-config controls to
suppress project instructions. The provider also skips its own project config
metadata reads when this flag is set; global config still applies. It cannot
remove instruction text that a host has already included in the supplied prompt
([`loadMergedConfig`](src/context/rules.ts)).

Truthy values: `1` or `true` (case-insensitive), same as OpenCode.

Instruction URL fetching and redirect policy belong to the host; this provider
has no separate instruction-fetch policy.

### Out of Scope

| Category | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| **Sandbox escapes** | The host permission system is not a sandbox (see above) |
| **Cursor / LLM data handling** | Data sent to Cursor is governed by Cursor's policies and your account terms |
| **MCP server behavior** | External MCP servers you configure are outside our trust boundary |
| **Malicious project config** | Users control their own configuration; trusted project `instructions` reading absolute/`~/` paths is expected OpenCode parity (see above) |
| **Host tool execution after user approval** | Actions the host runs under its normal permission prompts are expected behavior |

## Reporting Security Issues

Do not report a suspected vulnerability in a public GitHub issue, discussion, or pull request.

Use GitHub's private [vulnerability reporting form](https://github.com/oakimov/cursor-opencode-provider/security/advisories/new). This keeps the report and subsequent discussion private between the reporter and the repository maintainers.

Include the affected version, environment (OpenCode 1.x vs 2.x, plugin entrypoint), impact, reproduction steps, and any suggested mitigation. The initial message should not include credentials, personal data, or exploit code beyond what is needed to reproduce the issue. If the report requires sensitive supporting material, first send a minimal description and ask the maintainers to coordinate a suitable transfer method.

Reports must describe a concrete, reproducible security impact. Automated scanner output or model-generated speculation without validation may not receive a response.

We will make a reasonable effort to acknowledge valid reports, but we cannot promise a specific response or remediation timeline.
